name: Ebal
overview: The name Ebal appears both as a person and a significant location in Scripture. Ebal is mentioned as a son of Joktan and a Horite, indicating a genealogical and tribal identity (Genesis 36:23). More prominently, Mount Ebal is the site where half of the tribes of Israel stood to pronounce the curses of the law, in contrast to Mount Gerizim where blessings were declared (Deuteronomy 11:29; 27:12-13). Joshua later built an altar on Mount Ebal, and the people assembled there in obedience to Moses' command, underscoring the mountain's role in covenant renewal and the public affirmation of God's law (Joshua 8:30, 33).
